title: As Allen & Overy Deploys GPT-based Legal App Harvey Firmwide, Founders Say Other Firms Will Soon Follow
author: Bob Ambrogi

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Associate training: Automation threatens expertise reproduction
st.an: The source focuses on training Harvey’s model, protecting client confidentiality and claimed hallucination reductions. Its analogy to associate education acknowledges the importance of firm-specific knowledge, but it does not assess whether automation erodes human apprenticeship, creates a verification-expertise paradox or requires reconstructed associate training.

st.t: Agentic infrastructure: Harvey tests vertical vendor durability

It also preserves the cluster’s caution: these figures establish uptake, not accuracy, productivity gains, durable advantage or broader structural change.

kp.k: Allen & Overy deploys generative AI across global practice
kp.d: Ambrogi reports in 2023 that Allen & Overy integrated Harvey into its global practice for use by more than 3,500 lawyers across 43 offices operating in multiple languages. The article describes Harvey as using GPT-3, explicitly not ChatGPT, to support document creation and legal research through natural-language instructions. A&O describes itself as the first law firm using generative AI based on OpenAI's GPT models; Ambrogi says that claim appears true.
qs: Harvey uses the GPT-3 technology (*not* ChatGPT) to enable lawyers to create legal documents or perform legal research by providing simple instructions using natural language.
Allen & Overy (A&O) now describes itself as “the first law firm to use generative AI that’s based on OpenAI’s GPT models.”

kp.k: Trial reports substantial usage across languages and practices
kp.d: A&O says its trial began in November and that, by its conclusion, some 3,500 lawyers had submitted around 40,000 queries for daily client work. Harvey's founders additionally report use in 50 languages and 250 practice areas across all A&O offices. Pereyra describes daily usage approaching a fourth of the firm and monthly usage of about 80%. These are reported adoption figures rather than measured productivity outcomes.
qs: A&O said it began a trial of Harvey in November. By the end of the trial, some 3,500 A&O lawyers had asked Harvey around 40,000 queries for their day-to-day client work.
Pereyra  and Weinberg added that A&O had used Harvey in 50 different languages and 250 practice areas across all of its offices.
“It’s almost a fourth of the firm daily and about 80% of the firm monthly,” Pereyra said.

kp.k: A&O trial leader anticipates transformative efficiency gains
kp.d: David Wakeling, A&O partner and head of the Markets Innovation Group that led the trial, characterizes Harvey as a game-changer capable of transforming legal services through multilingual, cross-practice capabilities. His statements describe enthusiasm and anticipated benefits, with trial results characterized qualitatively rather than quantified.
qs: “It is a game-changer that can unleash the power of generative AI to transform the legal industry. Harvey can work in multiple languages and across diverse practice areas, delivering unprecedented efficiency and intelligence. In our trial, we saw some amazing results.”

kp.k: Founders predict further practice-specific and firmwide deployments
kp.d: Harvey founders Winston Weinberg and Gabriel Pereyra tell Ambrogi they are working with unnamed firms preparing deployments, some in selected practices and others firmwide. They leave announcements to those firms and expect further partnership and capability announcements within the next few months. At publication, these deployments remain reported plans rather than named, completed implementations.
qs: But they said that some of the firms will deploy it for specific practices, while others, as A&O did, will deploy it firmwide.

“I think other firms will adopt it in piecemeal, while others might also follow A&O’s path, so we’re letting these firms lead it and just working closely with them to develop this in parallel with them,” Pereyra said.
But they expect to have several new announcements of partnerships and capabilities coming within the next few months.

kp.k: Layered training tailors AI to firms and matters
kp.d: The founders describe training on at least three types of data: the GPT model's general internet data, general legal data such as case law and reference materials, and firm-specific historical work product and templates. Additional fine-tuning can specialize models for a client, litigation or transaction. Pereyra compares these stages to schooling, law school and learning a firm's distinctive practice; this is an analogy for model development, not a claim about changes to lawyer training.
qs: Pereyra and Weinberg said that Harvey is trained over at least three types of data.

Harvey is then further trained against general legal data, such as case law and reference materials. Finally, it is fine tuned against the law firm’s own data, such as its historical work product, templates, and the like.

“You can even specialize it more than that, where you can get specific models for cases — you can have a case where you can have a specific client matter or specific litigation and the model is fine tuned for that litigation or transaction.”
Harvey’s firm-specific training is like teaching an associate the firm’s unique practice.

kp.k: Confidentiality requires separation between firms and client matters
kp.d: The founders say a firm's trained model remains exclusive to it rather than becoming the base model for another firm's deployment. They also describe permissions and firewalls separating models within a firm to prevent cross-client leakage. Pereyra presents attorney feedback as a source of firm-specific model improvement and differentiation.
qs: To respect confidentiality, once Harvey is trained for a specific firm, that model stays specific to that firm and is not used as a base model when deploying Harvey at a different firm.
Any training that A&O does on their model just makes their model better.

“You can’t just take all of A&O’s client matters and use the same model because you don’t want leakage, even within the same firm, across client matters, so we’re being extremely careful of firewalling off all of these different things,” Weinberg said.

kp.k: Founders claim fine-tuning nearly eliminates context-specific hallucinations
kp.d: Pereyra and Weinberg assert that fine-tuning dramatically reduces fabricated answers and nearly eliminates them in highly context-specific applications. For contract review, they claim hallucinations fall essentially to zero; Pereyra further claims an error rate below that of a contract attorney. The article provides no test design or numerical comparison supporting those assertions and reports that the product was still not being demonstrated publicly.
qs: Pereyra and Weinberg say that Harvey’s method of fine tuning the AI dramatically reduces occurrences of hallucinations and, in highly context-specific applications, eliminates them almost entirely.
For contract review, for example, Harvey is able to reduce hallucinations “basically to zero.”
In fact, Pereyra said, the error rate is lower than for review by a contract attorney.
Meanwhile, Pereyra and Weinberg say they are still not demonstrating the product publicly.

kp.k: Firm-specific customization conditions the pace of vendor expansion
kp.d: The founders say they will continue deploying Harvey firm by firm because each implementation requires fine-tuning. Their stated approach deliberately limits expansion speed to allow sufficient attention to each firm.
qs: Pereyra and Weinberg said that they will continue to roll out Harvey on a firm-by-firm basis, as the model requires them to fine tune it for each firm.
“We’re trying to not scale too fast just because we want to make sure that we’re giving enough time to each firm.”

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Ambrogi reports firmwide deployment of Harvey at Allen & Overy; Harvey’s founders predict additional practice-specific and firmwide deployments.
pts.d: Ambrogi describes Harvey as using GPT-3, rather than ChatGPT, to let lawyers draft legal documents and conduct legal research through natural-language instructions. He reports that A&O has integrated it into its global practice for use by more than 3,500 lawyers across 43 offices. Interviewed founders Gabriel Pereyra and Winston Weinberg say they are working with other firms preparing deployments, but do not identify those firms. Pereyra anticipates varying adoption patterns rather than universally immediate firmwide adoption.

pts.k: A&O trial leader David Wakeling claims Harvey can transform legal work through multilingual, cross-practice efficiency and intelligence.
pts.d: The article quotes Wakeling, an A&O partner and head of the Markets Innovation Group that led the trial, describing transformative potential and unusually strong results. This is Wakeling’s assessment based on the trial and his legal-technology experience, rather than a quantified finding of productivity improvement.

pts.k: Pereyra and Weinberg describe firm- and matter-specific AI systems whose capabilities reflect proprietary work product and lawyer feedback, with separation intended to protect confidentiality.
pts.d: The founders say Harvey combines general GPT training, additional legal training, and firm-specific fine-tuning on historical work product and templates, with optional client- or matter-specific tuning. Pereyra claims lawyer feedback will make each firm’s model better or at least different from other firms’ models. They describe firm-level separation and internal permissions and firewalls to prevent information leakage across firms and client matters.

pts.k: The founders claim fine-tuning sharply reduces hallucinations; Pereyra claims contract-review errors are lower than those of a contract attorney.
pts.d: Ambrogi attributes the general hallucination-reduction claim to both founders and the comparison with human contract review specifically to Pereyra. The near-elimination claim is conditional on highly context-specific applications, with contract review given as the example; it is not stated as a universal absence of hallucinations across all legal tasks.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: Reported A&O trial usage provides concrete adoption evidence; claims about transformation, confidentiality architecture and accuracy rely on participant accounts rather than published comparative tests.
pts.d: A&O reports approximately 40,000 queries by some 3,500 lawyers during the trial. The founders add usage across 50 languages and 250 practice areas, with nearly one-quarter of the firm using Harvey daily and approximately 80% monthly. These figures describe breadth and frequency of use, not measured time savings or accuracy. Wakeling invokes 15 years of legal-technology experience and trial results without supplying outcome measurements. Additional deployments, customization, firewalls and hallucination reduction are described by the founders. The article supplies no benchmark, sample size, test methodology or numerical human-comparison result for the accuracy claims, and notes that the product is not yet being demonstrated publicly.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The 2023 article reports a completed trial beginning the preceding November, an announced deployment, and further announcements anticipated within months; expansion is deliberately firm-specific and paced.
pts.d: A&O’s integration announcement occurred the day before the article, following a trial begun in November. Other firms are described as preparing deployments, while partnership and capability announcements are expected within the next few months, without a fixed deployment schedule. The founders condition rollout on spending sufficient time fine-tuning for each firm. Accuracy claims are qualified by task specificity, and confidentiality is described as depending on segregated models, permissions and firewalls.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The direct subjects are A&O’s global lawyers, other prospective law-firm adopters and their clients; contract attorneys serve as an accuracy comparator.
pts.d: Lawyers are described as gaining a natural-language tool for drafting, research and contract review across languages and practice areas. Firms receive customized systems shaped by their own work product and attorney feedback, with rollout either practice-specific or firmwide. Clients’ documents and matters are implicated in customization and confidentiality protections. Harvey is the software provider, not an alternative legal service provider delivering the underlying legal work. The article does not predict lawyer job losses, staffing changes, fee changes or access-to-justice effects; its comparison with contract attorneys concerns errors rather than an explicit replacement forecast.
